subject: Hosted API latency SLO — proposed measurement windows and carveouts
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@fincorp.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinCorp Procurement <procurement@fincorp.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:13:00 -08:00
Subject: Hosted API SLO ask and evidence request

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — FinCorp platform team was impressed with the throughput and caching notes. Procurement asked me to circle back with a concrete request so we can align on the SLA language in the SOW.

High level asks:
- Firm latency commitments for the Hosted API (p50 and p95) per request for our primary model route.
- How you define the measurement window (rolling minute/1-hour/day aggregation) and how monthly compliance will be calculated.
- Carveouts: maintenance windows, regional outages, large burst traffic events.
- Evidence package we can use in procurement: sample traces, canary run summaries, and a small example of how you compute p95 across measurement buckets.

As a point of comparison, our internal target is p50 <= 120ms and p95 <= 600ms for critical routes during US-business hours. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to that, or propose an alternative and explain measurement logic?

We need a vendor-friendly spec by end of next week to keep our procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Integrations, FinCorp
elena.soto@fincorp.com
From: aisha_rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@fincorp.com>
Cc: FinCorp Procurement <procurement@fincorp.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 15:28:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLO ask and evidence request

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. High level response below; I attached a one-page SLO spec (SLO_Spec_FinCorp_v1.pdf) and a small evidence sample.

Proposal (Hostend API, primary model route):
- Commitment: p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 800ms (measured at the request boundary for the route).
- Measurement: rolling 1-hour buckets; each 1-hour bucket produces a p50/p95 value. Monthly compliance: we count the number of 1-hour buckets in the month where the p95 met the committed threshold. The monthly SLA is satisfied if >= 99% of 1-hour buckets meet p95 target. (This prevents short-lived spikes from rolling a whole month into breach.)
- Dayparting: Business hours (09:00–18:00 US/Eastern) vs off-hours. We propose the committed numbers above apply to business hours; off-hours will have a relaxed p95 of 1200ms (to reflect maintenance and lower priority background traffic).
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows (documented 48h in advance) are excluded; emergency maintenance and provider-level outages will be handled under the incident/fallback playbook. Large burst events are treated as follows: if 15-min sustained RPS exceeds the provisioned burst threshold by >3x and we detect a clear traffic-shaping event, affected 1-hour buckets are eligible for temporary carveout review (requires evidence).
- Evidence: sample traces and rolling-bucket exports attached (evidence_sample_traces.csv). We can provide access to per-token breakdowns and histogram data for audit.

Next steps I propose:
1) If FinCorp is OK with the numbers above, we’ll ship a SOW appendix with the exact measurement language and DocuSign link.
2) If you want tighter numbers (p50 120ms / p95 600ms), we can explore a Dedicated or reserved-capacity plan or a hybrid routing policy that pins your critical routes to higher-priority instances — we can cost that out in the SOW.

I know procurement needs timing; I can loop in Legal & Support for redlines and onboarding specifics.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
aisha.rahman@redwood.ai
Attachments: SLO_Spec_FinCorp_v1.pdf, evidence_sample_traces.csv

Notes / questions:
- Marissa: procurement will push for firm penalties; what’s our standard cap on SLA credits? Can we accept the rolling 1-hour aggregation language? Any wording you want added around force majeure or provider dependencies?
- Ben: operationally, can Support provide the requested evidence package for the POC? Also, if they insist on 120/600 for hosted, what mitigations (reserved capacity, warm-cold routing, smaller model quantization) are realistic without Dedicated?

Aisha / Ben —

High level: rolling 1-hour bucket approach is standard and we can accept it, but procurement will request clear examples in the SOW (we should include the sample CSV and a short section that calculates a toy month to demonstrate the 99% bucket rule).

On penalties: propose standard credit cap equal to 3 months of hosting fees for the route (we can reduce to 1 month for pilot accounts). We should add explicit carveout language for scheduled maintenance and regional cloud provider incidents — keep emergency maintenance defined narrowly.

Ben — please confirm operational ability to deliver the evidence_package and whether Support can run a 24-hour canary with per-bucket exports before signature. If we need to hit 120/600 for business hours we should price a reserved-capacity addendum.

I’ll start the SOW appendix draft and include a DocuSign placeholder.

-marissa
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Hosted API SLO ask and evidence request — SOW appendix and next steps

Elena —

Thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Quick summary and next steps: 

Committed SLO (business hours 09:00–18:00 US/Eastern):
- p50 <= 150ms per request
- p95 <= 800ms per request
Measurement & compliance:
- Measured on rolling 1-hour buckets; monthly compliance requires >= 99% of 1-hour buckets to meet the p95 threshold.
Carveouts / exceptions:
- Scheduled maintenance (documented 48 hours in advance)
- Provider-level region outage (we will provide incident ID and root cause timelines)
- Verified traffic-shaping bursts >3x provisioned RPS (requires joint review and evidence)

If FinCorp requires the tighter p50 120ms / p95 600ms for business hours, we can grant that under a reserved-capacity addendum (pricing TBD). I attached the SOW appendix draft (SOW_Draft_FinCorp.docx) and the SLO spec PDF for procurement language. Evidence samples included.

Please review and if acceptable we’ll send a DocuSign SOW appendix for signature and schedule a 24-hour canary the week of Feb 23 to produce live bucketed metrics for your team to audit.

Next immediate steps:
1) Procurement: confirm whether the committed numbers above are sufficient, or request reserved-capacity pricing for the tighter SLO.
2) FinCorp Platform: confirm a date for the canary (we need a 24-hour window and an expected RPS profile).
3) Redwood Legal: I’ve looped Marissa for the appendix and penalty cap language.

Best regards,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
